oublierEx.introTitre: How long to get over your ex?
oublierEx.introTexte: Answer based on what you're living today, not on what you'd like to feel. The test starts from twenty simple things (your relationship, the breakup, how you feel, what you do with your days) and estimates, in months, how long it will still take you to move on.
oublierEx.resultatLibelle: Based on your answers, you'll still need
oublierEx.levierTitre: What would save you the most time
oublierEx.levierTexte: {{facteur}}: with "{{reponse}}", the estimate would drop to {{apres}} instead of {{avant}}.
oublierEx.levierTexteMulti: With these {{n}} changes, the estimate would drop to {{apres}} instead of {{avant}}:
oublierEx.partage: {{duree}} more to get over my ex, according to the test
oublierEx.r1_d: Your ex already takes up little space in your days, and what's left should fade in the coming weeks. You've done the hardest part, even if a song or a date can still sting now and then.
oublierEx.r1_a: Don't stir anything up now: no texting “just to see how they're doing”, no stories watched late at night. That's often when people relapse over nothing.
oublierEx.r2_d: You're on the right track. The breakup still hurts at times, but you already have what you need around you to move forward. Look at what's holding you back above: it's often a single habit that drags things out.
oublierEx.r2_a: Pick just one thing to change this week, the one the test points to. Just one, but stick to it.
oublierEx.r3_t: Less than a year, if you go about it right
oublierEx.r3_d: Your relationship mattered, and it still takes up a lot of space. That's normal: this kind of breakup takes time, and nobody gets over it in a few weeks. But part of that time depends on what you do now.
oublierEx.r3_a: Start with what keeps your ex in your days, like the texts you reread at night or their stories. That's where you'll gain the most.
oublierEx.r4_t: More than a year, if nothing changes
oublierEx.r4_d: The breakup hit you hard, and several things are making it last. It's not a matter of willpower: when the relationship was long, the ending caught you off guard, or your ex is still around one way or another, detaching takes longer.
oublierEx.r4_a: Don't stay alone with this. Talk to the people close to you, and if it keeps you from sleeping or working, to a professional. Then tackle the point shown above.
oublierEx.r5_t: Your relationship is still holding you back a lot
oublierEx.r5_d: With what you're going through today, the page will have a hard time turning on its own. This number is about your current situation, not about you: the habits that keep your ex in your life, or hoping they'll come back. And those can change.
oublierEx.r5_a: Start with the point shown above, stick to it for three months, then take the test again. And if you feel like you've been going round in circles for a long time, a therapist can help you move forward much faster.
